vulnerability.name: Java Unauthenticated Remote JMX Code Execution
vulnerability.author: SecGen pipeline
vulnerability.description: A small long-running Java process is run as an unprivileged service user with the JMX management agent exposed remotely and misconfigured: com.sun.management.jmxremote.authenticate=false and ssl=false, bound on the configured port (default 1099) with java.rmi.server.hostname set to the VM's address so the RMI stub is reachable. With authentication disabled a remote client can register a javax.management.loading.MLet MBean, load a ClassLoader from an attacker-served HTTP URL and invoke it, running arbitrary Java in the JVM as the service user. OpenJDK 17 (Debian 12) still ships the deprecated MLet class the attack relies on. The Metasploit module exploit/multi/misc/java_jmx_server automates the MLet load; because it serves the payload over HTTP, the target JVM must be able to reach the attacker's SRVHOST.
vulnerability.hint: A Java service listens on an RMI port; its JMX management agent accepts connections without authentication.
